reason: Only the minimum Node.js version rises (engines >=18 to >=20); there is no API change and the template already runs Node 22.

The pinned stripe 23.0.0 no longer sends 2026-07-29.dahlia: later bumps (22.6.0 to 2026-08-26.dahlia, 23.0.0 to 2026-09-30.endive, each its own population entry) superseded it, so this bump's behavior isn't in the pinned version.

Tried a retry/classify-errors task against a local stub that cuts the body off: the natural code (treat StripeConnectionError as transient) works better on 23.0.0, nothing plausible catches StripeAPIError for a dropped connection, and on 22.2.0 the default Node client hung instead of throwing StripeAPIError (only the fetch client threw it).

geography is only @deprecated in the .d.ts and openai 7.39.0 emits no runtime warning; TypeScript (checked with typescript-6's suggestion diagnostics) reports the tag only on a property-access write like params.geography = ..., not on the object-literal argument projects.create({ name, geography }) that code actually writes, so a stale variant goes unsignalled.

Tried passing Stripe.AddressParam / Stripe.JapanAddressParam values to v2 accounts create/update (customer shipping, identity individual and business details, merchant support): the new operation-specific interfaces are structurally identical (same optional fields), so the code compiles and behaves the same on 23.0.0 as on 22.2.0.

Behavior on malformed input only: an invalid Date serializes to the same '0NaN-NaN-…' string on 8.21.0 and 8.23.1 (only a PG_INVALID_DATE warning is added), which Postgres rejects as a timestamp, so no working code could have depended on passing one.

The field is removed from the types 'to match the API response': the API already omitted name on response.function_call_arguments.done before the cutoff (openai-java #682, January 2026), so code reading event.name on 6.39.1 compiled but got undefined, and a stale variant fails on the old version too.

Tried sending one attachment stream to several recipients and a stream destroyed mid-send (streamTransport): on 8.0.10 the reused stream went out as an empty attachment and the destroyed one hung forever, so no working pre-cutoff code depended on the old behavior; 10.1.7 now fails those sends (ESTREAM / premature close).

Checked with a local SMTP stub that advertises STARTTLS and AUTH, refuses STARTTLS (454) and requires AUTH: 8.0.10 with opportunisticTLS already skips AUTH after the refusal (it never parsed the plaintext EHLO's AUTH line) and fails with 530, exactly like 10.1.7, so code written for the old version could never have relied on plaintext authentication there.
